title: Tax and Jurisdictional Compliance
answer: Structuring, transfer pricing, research credits, indirect tax and audit defence.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Tax Structuring and Planning
children.blurb: Tax structuring and planning covers the design of a group's legal entities, contracts and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance of a business.

children.name: Transfer Pricing
children.blurb: Transfer pricing is the set of rules and methods that decide how prices are set for goods, services, loans and intellectual property moving between related companies in different tax jurisdictions.

children.name: Research Credits from Engineering Records
children.blurb: Research credits from engineering records covers the practice of reconstructing a claim for research and development tax relief out of the artefacts a software or AI team already produces.

children.name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
children.blurb: Sales, use and value added tax covers the transaction taxes charged on goods and services, as distinct from taxes on income or profit.

children.name: Audit Defence and Controversy
children.blurb: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of responding to a tax authority's questions, from the first information request through formal dispute and, where it applies, litigation or competent authority proceedings.

sections.body: Tax and jurisdictional compliance is the work of fitting a company's operations, contracts and records to the tax rules of every place it touches. Artificial intelligence is being used on the document side of that work: reading invoices, intercompany agreements, engineering logs and correspondence, then sorting and flagging what a tax team would otherwise read by hand. In transfer pricing it helps assemble comparables and check that the story told by contracts matches the story told by the numbers. In indirect tax it classifies transactions and tests them against rate and exemption rules that differ by jurisdiction. In audit defence it reconstructs timelines and pulls the specific records a revenue authority has asked about. The output is a draft, a flag or a summary that a qualified person still has to review.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The parts that are largely solved are retrieval and consistency: finding every invoice with a given treatment, checking that a policy was applied the same way across entities, and turning unstructured records into a clean table. What is not solved is judgment. Whether an arrangement has economic substance, whether a comparable is truly comparable, and whether a credit claim survives scrutiny are questions that turn on facts and on the law of a specific jurisdiction, and models do not settle them. Rules change constantly and by location, so any system needs maintenance and a clear record of which version of a rule it applied. Confidentiality and privilege matter here more than in most fields, because the inputs are the company's own sensitive filings. The honest limit is that these tools narrow the reading and preparation load, and they can be confidently wrong in ways that are hard to spot without a specialist.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run from planning through to dispute. Tax Structuring and Planning is the entry point, covering how an operating model is shaped and where the compliance questions begin. Transfer Pricing takes the cross border piece, where the pricing of intercompany dealings has to be supported and documented. Research Credits from Engineering Records sits alongside it, showing how technical and engineering material is turned into evidence for a credit claim. Sales, Use and Value Added Tax covers the transaction level taxes that touch everyday invoicing and reporting. Audit Defence and Controversy is where all of it converges, because an examination tests whether the structuring, the pricing, the credit and the indirect tax positions hold together under scrutiny. A reader would start with structuring for the overall shape, go to transfer pricing or indirect tax for the specific regime in front of them, use the research credits page when the question is about evidence from technical work, and finish with audit defence to see how the earlier choices are examined.
